# UI kit

The shared components every page and module builds with (`src/platform/ui/`): what they do beyond
their props, and which values they share with the CSS. Props, variants and where each is used:
[shared components reference](/docs/reference/components/README.md); rules and decided choices:
[component-set.md](/docs/ui/component-set.md). A change here reaches every page.

## How the pieces link

- `layoutSizes.ts` and `scrollMargin.ts` hold Tailwind classes that read CSS variables from `src/app/(frontend)/globals.css` (`--reading-width`, `--header-clearance`, `--anchor-offset`, `--chart-small-width`, `--chart-stack-width`), so each size is defined once (#616); `layoutSizes.test.ts` and `scrollMargin.test.ts` check the names.
- `Button` and `Link` render through `AppLink`: `next/link` for routes, a plain `<a>` for in-page `#` links so keyboard focus moves (`AppLink.tsx`). `LinkButton` (`CMSLink.tsx`) turns a resolved CMS link into a `Button`: appearance `outline` becomes `secondary`, `accent` the orange `accent` button, anything else `primary`.
- `Media` picks `VideoMedia` for a `video` mime type, else `ImageMedia` (`Media.tsx`). `getMediaUrl` keeps upload paths relative so Next optimizes them as local images, and the image's `updatedAt` is appended as its cache key (`ImageMedia.client.tsx`, `src/platform/lib/getMediaUrl.ts`).
- A chart's colours follow its parts' order, `chart-1` to `chart-6`, the [theme](/src/platform/theme/README.md)'s chart tokens; a chart whose spec says `palette: 'warm'` is drawn in orange and gray, by marking its root `data-chart-palette`, so no adapter changes; a seventh part throws (`src/platform/ui/chart/chartPalette.ts`), and the spec refuses it first (`src/platform/lib/chart/spec.ts`). `LegendSlot` and `SWATCH_COLOUR` in `Legend.tsx` are also fixed at six.
- A post's or an event's page heads with a plain `PageHeader` band (`variant="band"`: a themed surface under the site header, the category and the title) and shows its picture whole, never cropped, as `FeaturedImage` under the metadata bar, loading early, with its credit under it; with no picture nothing is drawn and no gap is left. The picture is full width above the text on a phone, half the column floated right from `md` and a third from `lg`, with the text wrapping beside it, and it has no Enlarge button and opens no dialog (the shared `Figure` with `zoom={false}`, so the picture starts on the text's first line, #1055). `ArticlePage` takes the picture as `image` and draws it after the metadata bar, in one box with the content that contains the float, so what follows a short text clears the picture; an article that opens with a row of cards shows them first and the picture starts beside the text after them, because a card row runs the whole column and can't sit beside a floated picture (`ArticlePage`'s `lead`, from `splitLeadingWideBlocks`); from `md` a panel or button beside it is a box of its own and takes the room left, and the text's `RichText` is given `besideFloat` so it flows beside the picture instead of staying narrow (`PageHeader.tsx`, `FeaturedImage.tsx`, `Figure.tsx`, `ArticlePage.tsx`, #1013, #1023, #1055).
- A post's or an event's metadata is the `MetaBar` above the picture: one thin line of labelled items (labels in the theme's `text-fine` size) with a hairline between them and no box, and one straight groove line (a dark hairline and the accent) directly under it across the whole column, the same at every width. An event's bar is `align="start"`: grouped at the left, from `md` one row on one text baseline, below it a two-column list above the line, and a place too long for one line cut with an ellipsis (capped at 20rem; it gives up width first, so the date stays on one line). A post's bar is `align="end"`: author and compact date only, in the `text-fine` size, one row at every width ending on the right edge, a long author name cut with an ellipsis, never wrapped. Either way the whole text of a cut value is in `title` and in the page. The line takes the width of what sits under it: a post's text, an event's panels (the whole column), and is hidden from assistive technology (`MetaBar.tsx`, `ArticlePage.tsx`'s `bylineAlign`, #1002, #1055).
- The title band can sit over a photo (`PageHeader` `variant="band"`, `backdrop`; `BandBackdrop`, #1024): one crop per screen size, phone under `md`, tablet from `md`, desktop from `lg` (the theme's breakpoints), each drawn by `Media` with `atFocalPoint`; a photo several sizes use is drawn once, and an image hidden at the current size is lazy so it is never fetched. The photo is `opacity-60` and `grayscale-50`, with a `--surface` scrim at 50% over it, so the title meets WCAG AA over any photo; the two strengths are `BAND_PHOTO_ALPHA` and `BAND_SCRIM_ALPHA` in the theme contract. It is absolutely placed inside the band, which then clips it (`relative overflow-hidden`), so the band's height does not change, and the text sits above it. A `BadgeList` with `plated` lays each badge on a solid surface plate, because a badge's tint is see-through. No crop, or an empty backdrop, draws exactly the plain band, with the same markup (`BandBackdrop.tsx`, `PageHeader.tsx`, `Badge.tsx`, `src/platform/lib/bandBackdrop.ts`).
- A picture that must stay cropped, such as the home page's hero photo, keeps its subject in view through the upload's focal point: `Media` with `atFocalPoint` sets the image's `object-position` from Payload's `focalX` and `focalY` (percent, centre when unset or out of range) through `toObjectPosition`. Cards never pass it and keep their centred crop. A focal point only chooses which part of a cropped picture shows, so it cannot keep an off-centre region such as a text panel out of every width: such a picture is shown whole (`ImageMedia.client.tsx`, `src/platform/lib/focalPoint.ts`, `PageHero.tsx`, #1013).
- `Field.Money` is a whole-dollar box: it groups the digits with commas after a dollar sign as the reader types, cuts cents (a pasted `$1,250,000.99` keeps `$1,250,000`), and keeps the caret after the digit just typed or deleted even when commas appear before it and, when the reader deletes a number's first digit, keeps the zeros left in front (`$00,000`) until the box loses focus, so the digit typed next replaces it and the number keeps its size (`FieldMoney.client.tsx`, `lib/money.ts`, #1035, #1172).
- `SegmentedControl` joins a few short options (two to three) into one small 36 px control with one border and divider lines, the picked option filled with the accent and `aria-pressed`; it is named by an `aria-label` or by a visible label (`labelledBy`), and each option is a `Button` drawn 36 px and tapped as 44 px (an invisible area past the box) (`SegmentedControl.tsx`, #1118). `Field` in the `bar` layout takes an `aside` for it, two children: a short label, centred over the control, on the line of the field's own label (which does not wrap and may run on under it), and the control beside the box, centred on it; the aside stacks under the box when the field is narrower than 16 rem, and the field's label drops to the smaller text under 20 rem. `Card` has an `xs` padding (12 px) for compact cards stacked on a phone's first screen. `CertaintyBadge` can say words of its own (a year's note) in the certainty's look.
- `Field` in the `bar` layout puts its `action` beside the box, or inside it with `actionPlacement="inside"` (#1110): the box draws the one border and the one focus ring, the action sits at the trailing end with the same 6 px inset above, below and at the end, and the border takes the accent while the action is not disabled. The check-mark inside it is a `Button` of the `action` variant (flat and muted while disabled, accent-colored and lifted by a shadow while enabled, no lift with reduced motion) and the `icon-sm` size, drawn 36 px and tapped as 44 px (`Field.client.tsx`, `Button.tsx`).
- A `Field` hands its one control its id, `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid` through one context; a control outside a `Field` throws (`fieldContext.ts`, `Field.client.tsx`).

## Behaviors

- A button with `loading` shows a spinner and ignores clicks but stays focusable (`aria-disabled`), so focus isn't lost (`Button.tsx`). `external` opens a new tab and adds spoken text saying so (`Button.tsx`, `Link.tsx`).
- Charts: `Chart` checks the spec, asks `chart/chartRegistry.ts` for an adapter, and draws the key, caption and numbers table around it. The first adapter that supports the kind draws it (`breakdown`: breakdown; `css`: units; `visx`: bar, stacked); the `text` adapter supports every kind and is last. Every adapter passes `chart/chartAdapter.contract.tsx`; chart libraries are allowed only under `chart/adapters/` (lint, `CHART_LIBRARIES` in `eslint.boundaries.config.mjs`).
- A bar or stacked chart (visx, #1206) is drawn large for readers who see poorly: names and values at about 18 and 16 units in a 320-unit drawing, so about 16px or more on a phone. Stacked (a phone, a narrow column) it fills the width up to 28rem (`--chart-stack-width`); from the chart container's `2xl` it is the 20rem thumbnail with its text beside it. The shared scale shows as short ticks at each bar, with no axis labels, since every bar prints its own value (`chart/adapters/visx/barLayout.ts`).
- A breakdown (#866) is drawn at full width, not as a thumbnail: a grid of squares worth a fixed dollar amount each (rounded to whole squares, largest remainder; `hideSquares` leaves out the grid, its key and the square value, so only the ranked bars show, #943), a key in dollars, ranked bars with the main pieces nested under their area in the area's colour, and the other pieces in one list under "See the smaller pieces", biggest first and coloured by their own rank. Colour follows size, from `chart-ramp-1` to `chart-ramp-7`; pale steps keep a thin outline and every figure is also text. Bar length is share times one shared scale, so a dollar is the same length in every breakdown (`chart/adapters/breakdown/`, `lib/chart/breakdown.ts`; the design reference is `docs/ui/reference/breakdown-chart-preview.html`).
- Every chart carries its numbers as a real table under "Show the numbers", closed by default, or for screen readers only when the chart is given `numbers="screen-reader"`, as in a fact tab (`chart/ChartDataTable.tsx`, #980). A chart can also leave its title and takeaway to screen readers (`heading="screen-reader"`), and draws no caption when it has nothing to say, so no gap is left. A drawing that gains from size is a thumbnail; `ChartZoom` is a thin caller of the shared `Zoom`, which moves the same server-rendered chart into a full-screen `Dialog` instead of copying it, and is the chart's only client code (`chart/ChartZoom.client.tsx`, `Zoom.client.tsx`). With scripting off the Enlarge button is hidden.
- `Figure` floats a small picture right from `md` (two fifths of the text column by default; `size` sets a third or half; `half-then-third` is the article picture's, #1023) and fills the column below. Its key, long caption and the larger picture show only in the `Zoom` dialog, never in the small view. A small expand icon (two arrows pointing apart, 44 px, on a dark translucent backing) sits over the picture's top-right corner instead of a text button, and a click or tap on the picture opens the same dialog; the icon is always shown, since touch has no hover, and is named "Enlarge: <title>" for screen readers; with scripting off it is hidden (`Figure.tsx`, `Zoom.client.tsx` `trigger="icon"`, #816, #1156). A chart keeps its Enlarge text button.
- `VersionCheck` (root layout) polls `/api/version` every 30 s, but only while the reader has been active in the last 30 s and the tab is visible, and again when the tab regains focus. The first answer is the baseline; a different build shows a toast with a Refresh button that reloads. A dismissed build isn't offered again; a newer one is. It does nothing when the server reports `development` (`VersionCheck.client.tsx`, `src/app/(frontend)/api/version/route.ts`).
- `AdminBar` is always mounted but hidden until Payload's bar reports a signed-in admin or editor (`isStaffRole`); residents see nothing (`AdminBar.client.tsx`, #203). `LivePreviewListener` refreshes the page when the editor saves in Live Preview; `[slug]/page.tsx` mounts it only in draft mode.
- `LoadMore` (`useLoadMore`, `LoadMoreFooter`) loads the next page by cursor shortly before the end, for 4 pages counting the first (`AUTO_LOAD_PAGES`); after that the reader clicks "Load more", so the footer stays reachable. The button is a real link to the next numbered page, so it works without JavaScript and in a new tab; a repeated item is dropped; if focus was on the button when the last load removed it, focus moves to the status line (`LoadMore.client.tsx`).
- The "On this page" menu needs at least 3 sections (`MIN_SECTIONS` in `onThisPage.ts`); the highlighted section is the last heading above a reading line taken from the heading's own scroll margin plus a little slack, so the heading a click lands on is the highlighted one.
- `MapEmbed` draws a live map only when `toGoogleMapsEmbedUrl` accepts the address (an `https` Google embed address). The frame is created only once the dialog opens, and with no valid address only the picture and text show. It fills the width it is given (`MapEmbed.client.tsx`, `src/platform/lib/googleMapsEmbed.ts`).
- `SidebarCTA` draws its sentence only when given one, with the heading's gap to the button widened to match, so a box whose heading and button already say it has no empty line (`SidebarCTA.tsx`, #1010).
- `Section` `placement="inline"` draws only its tone, with no container or padding, for a block inside a page section's cell (`Section.tsx`, #884).
- A `MetaList` value can shrink inside its row, so a clamped or truncated value stays on its line instead of widening the list (`MetaList.tsx`).
- `FORM_MESSAGES` are the fixed texts for a failed send ("offline", "failed"); each form adds only its own cases (`formMessages.ts`, #204).
- A `Disclosure` a reader opens is scrolled into view (#1152): the page moves just far enough to show the box's end with a small gap under it; a box taller than the screen stops with its summary row under the site header (and the "On this page" bar where there is one) instead, so the top wins; a box already in view moves nothing. Closing never scrolls, and neither does a box that is open when the page loads. A box can name an anchor, `revealAnchor` (the id of an element such as its card's heading): the page then scrolls as far as shows the box's end without the anchor going above the sticky header, and the anchor wins when both cannot show; the rule is `revealShift` and the scroll is `reveal.client.ts`, which a box that opens by itself calls too (#1178). Without an anchor the rule is the browser's own `scrollIntoView` with `block: 'nearest'`, measured from the box's scroll margins (`REVEAL_SCROLL_MARGIN` in `scrollMargin.ts`, which reads `--anchor-offset`), called from the summary row's click, the component's only client code, through `reveal.client.ts`. A box with another `Disclosure` directly under it (its next sibling element) also keeps room for that one's summary row and half a row more, so the reader sees there is more to open (#1154): the click measures that room and sets it on the box as `--reveal-peek` (`REVEAL_PEEK_VAR`), which the bottom scroll margin adds to its gap, so the top still wins when not all of it fits; a box with none under it keeps only the gap. Every look does it except `bar`, which is pinned under the site header. With scripting off the box still opens and closes, without the scroll (`Disclosure.tsx`, `DisclosureSummary.client.tsx`).
- Motion helpers (#1048, #1068): `prefersReducedMotion()` in `motion.client.ts`, and `useCountedNumber(target)`, which counts the shown number to a new target in 1.5 seconds (`COUNT_MS`; `YEAR_COUNT_MS`, half a second, is for a switch of tax year, #1087) and jumps at once with reduced motion; `useReplayProgress(run)` gives a fill's progress from 0 to 1 over one second (`FILL_MS`) each time `run` changes, starting and staying at 1 with reduced motion, so a row that opens can grow its bars and count its amounts with it (#1163); an optional `delayMs` holds it at 0 first, and `ScaledBreakdown` gives it `EXPAND_MS` (500 ms, the time a `listRow` takes to expand) so the fill starts as the row finishes opening (#1170). `holdScrollAnchor()` marks the page while a row expands or folds so the browser's scroll anchoring does not move the page with it. Both share `easeOut` from `motion.client.ts`. `ScaledBreakdown` takes `fillKey` (the bars grow with `chart-fill-x` and the amounts count up each time it changes, the percents unchanged, `valuesAt` in `lib/chart/breakdown.ts`; the growth restarts in place rather than redrawing the chart, which would make the browser's scroll anchoring move the page, and each counting amount keeps its final value's room, so nothing reflows, #1165) and `compact` (thinner bars, for a breakdown inside a bill). `Disclosure` takes `onOpening`, called from the summary's click while the box is still closed, so the caller's content is ready before it shows (#1165; not on the pinned `bar`). A `ShareBill` slice can carry a `shortName`: below 24 rem the rest of its name hides, kept for screen readers (#1163).
- `ShareBill` draws one whole as a bill (#1196): the title on top with no amount, then one row for every slice, in the order given: its name, its percent and its dollars (the percents in one column, the dollars flush right in their own with a clear gap between the two, #1163, #1184), and under them the slice's own bar in its tone (`shareTones.ts`: the City's slice the solid primary green, the others neutral tones of different lightness), drawn like the City breakdown's rows. The bars share one scale, the largest slice's, and every row is built the same way (no colour square, no fill, no rule of its own, 20 px of text on one line down to 320 px, smaller type and tighter columns under 24 rem), so the rows and bars sit level. The total is the last row (bold, under a stronger rule; it flashes the accent once each time `pulseKey` changes, for `TOTAL_PULSE_MS`, 0.3 seconds, which the `total-pulse` animation holds equal, #1051, #1182). The receipt is one grid of three columns, the name and two right-aligned columns kept on one line: the dollar column is at least wide enough for a four-digit amount and grows to the widest amount, the total's included, so a large home's figures never run into the names, and the percent column is fixed; the rows and the total share one grid (`subgrid`), so each column lines up from row to row and the total's amount ends under the rows' dollars with nothing under the percents (#1163). The caller writes the label for screen readers, the rows' list name (`ShareBill.tsx`, #1111). `nested` puts extra content as a row of its own directly under one slice's row, set in from the left with a line in the City's colour down its side, and its amounts set in from the right by about the dollar column's width (`NESTED_AMOUNTS_INSET`, which the row's button does not take), so the amounts inside end before the bodies' amounts and are not read as parts of the sum, such as the whole bill's closed breakdown row under the City (#1163).
- `Tabs` draws its tab buttons plain and equal (#1112): one row sharing the width equally, each at least 48 px tall with the label centred on one line, a small gap between them (smaller type, spacing and padding on a phone so a label of the editor's limit keeps room at 320 px) and the panel under the row in its own border, not joined to it. The selected tab has the primary border, a soft primary fill and a bolder label; the others are quiet. Every use gets this look, since it lives in `Tabs.client.tsx` alone; a tab's `trigger` is a short label, with visually hidden text after it if screen readers need more (`Tabs.client.tsx`).
- `Tabs` gives every tab a link of its own (#1097), on for every tabbed block with no setting: choosing a tab puts `#<anchor>` in the address (the item's `anchor`, else its `value`), replacing the history entry so Back leaves the page; opening an address that names a tab, or the address changing on the page, opens that tab and scrolls the tabs into view below the header; a name that is no tab changes nothing, and the first tab is shown. A tabbed block whose names repeat those of an earlier block on the page numbers them `-2`, `-3`, so every tab on a page has a link of its own.
- `ScaledBreakdown` draws a breakdown chart in the browser with every amount multiplied by a factor, from the same drawing code as `Chart`'s breakdown, so the City's tax split follows the home value a reader types. It takes a spec the server already checked and never parses it, so no chart library and no spec rules (zod) reach the browser (`chart/ScaledBreakdown.tsx`, `lib/chart/scale.ts`, #1020). `ChartCaption` is the caption under a chart, shared by both. Its `title` can be kept for screen readers only when a heading above already says it; the takeaway always shows (#1144). `hideSource` leaves the as-of line and the source links out of the caption (the Estimate badge and fine print stay) for a page that lists them elsewhere (#1180).
- `ProgressBar` is a native `<progress>` with a required `label` for screen readers; its fill comes from the element's own value (no inline style), a value is kept between 0 and `max`, and a `max` of 0 shows an empty bar. Callers always write the numbers beside it (`ProgressBar.tsx`, #939).
- `AreaChart` (#1190) draws a series over days as a smooth curve (`lib/smoothPath.ts`, monotone, so it never dips below a flat stretch or the baseline) with a soft fill, a faint baseline, the first, middle and last day written under it (the last reads "Today") and a marker on the latest value, in `done` or `open` (`success`) tokens. `max` is shared by pictures read side by side, `fromZero={false}` starts a running total at its lowest value so its shape shows, a series of zeros or a `max` of 0 is the flat baseline, one value is a dot, and a value above `max` stays inside. It has a text `label` listing every value for screen readers; the caller always writes the figure beside it. Server-rendered, no client code (`AreaChart.tsx`).
- `HeatMap` shows how much happened each day as squares, darker for more: `week` is a full-width strip with weekday letters, `calendar` is Monday rows that fill the width of their box, named by their Monday, with days to come dashed; the last day is ringed, a zero is a faint square, and its `label` lists every value for screen readers (`HeatMap.tsx`, #1191). With a `selection` the days become buttons that say whether they are pressed, the map is a group instead of an image, today's ring gives way to the ring on a pressed day, and a day that is not enabled is a muted, slashed square that can't be pressed and says why (`HeatCell.tsx`, #1204). `today` moves the ring to another day or takes it off, and `toCome={false}` leaves the days after the last one empty instead of dashed, for a period that is over (#1218). An optional `caption` adds a line under the squares with the caption at the left and a Less-to-More key of the same shades at the right, on one line at every width (#1205, #1217).
- `Dialog` is a full-screen `sheet` by default; `placement="center"` is a panel over a dimmed page. `RouteDialog` is an always-open centered `Dialog` for an intercepted route: its close button, back button and Escape all call `router.back()` (`Dialog.client.tsx`, `RouteDialog.client.tsx`, #946).
- `Badge` has `open` (green) and `done` (purple) marks, each with words and an icon from the caller, and `outline` for a plain label (`Badge.tsx`, #946). `size` is `sm` (the default), `xs` (tighter padding, for a badge that shares a row with a label, #1118) or `md`, with larger words and icon; the plan's Open, Done and Not planned marks use `md` and its labels stay small (#952).
- `Alert` announces itself unless `live={false}`: errors interrupt, other tones wait their turn (`Alert.tsx`); the `info` tone is blue, from the `info` and `info-strong` theme tokens (#818).

## Shared pieces it uses

- Related notes: [theme](/src/platform/theme/README.md) (chart tokens; its `ThemeSelector` uses `Field`), [rich text](/src/platform/richtext/README.md) (renders charts and blocks with the kit, and the "On this page" menu), [shared Payload code](/src/platform/payload/README.md) (`AdminBar` reads `isStaffRole`).
- Helpers from `src/platform/lib/` (`cn`, `getMediaUrl`, chart `spec`/`table`, `googleMapsEmbed`, `getURL`) and `src/platform/payload/roles.ts`; `@/cssVariables` and `@/imageQualities` for images.

## Rules and the tests that protect them

- Pages and modules use the kit, never raw `a`, `button`, `input`, `select`, `textarea`, `details`, `summary` or `img`; the native element lives inside a kit component (guard rail 2). Lint bans them outside `src/platform/ui/` (`eslint.ui-kit.config.mjs`).
- `Disclosure`'s arrow is `size-5` in the main text colour on the `card` and `row` looks, so it reads clearly in light and dark mode (#1136). It has five looks: `card`, `row` (no box of its own, only side padding: a few rows go in one `Card` with `divide-y`, split by lines, so a closed row is only as tall as its summary, #1111, #1118), `listRow` (a row inside a list: a tinted, borderless button-like summary with a `text-list-row` label a little larger than the list's rows and a `size-5` arrow in the link colour, so it reads as clickable, no outer padding, so the list places it, a body back in body text with no rule above it (#1196), and an expansion over 500 ms instead of a snap, with the scroll that shows a box a reader opened waiting until the expansion ends, #1163, #1170), `bar` and `link`. A `Disclosure` chevron turns only for its own box, so boxes can nest: `Disclosure.test.tsx` runs the real Tailwind output against a nested and a top-level box (#967).
- Sizes and scroll margins read one variable each: `layoutSizes.test.ts`, `scrollMargin.test.ts`.
- The registry's order and the text fallback: `chart/chartRegistry.test.ts`; every adapter's markup (no `style`, no colour literals, real text, axe): `chart/chartAdapter.contract.test.tsx`.
- Chart libraries stay in the adapters: `chart/chartLibraries.lint.test.ts`; the browser never gets a library or the spec rules through the zoom: `chart/ChartZoom.imports.test.ts`.
- Chart colours, the six-part limit and the seven-step ramp: `chart/chartPalette.test.ts`; the breakdown: `chart/adapters/breakdown/breakdownAdapter.test.tsx`.
- Each component's behavior and accessibility: its `*.test.tsx` beside it (`Button`, `Link`, `Field.client`, `LoadMore.client`, `MapEmbed.client`, `AdminBar.client`, `OnThisPage.client`, `Dialog.client`, `Toast`, `ProgressBar`, `RouteDialog.client` and others).

## Boundaries

- It imports only from `src/platform/` and no module (0008; no file here imports `@/modules`). `index.ts` exports the small primitives; larger ones are imported by file so a client component that needs a Button doesn't bundle them (`index.ts`).

## Decisions

[0008](/docs/architecture/decisions/0008-compose-modules-at-the-app-level.md), [0018](/docs/architecture/decisions/0018-charts-behind-our-own-port.md).

## Known gaps

- Tone names differ across `Alert`, `Badge` and `Card` (#769).
- `VersionCheck` has no test of its own.
- `PeriodNav` is a title with a button on each side that steps to the period before and the one after, such as the month a calendar shows; the caller holds the state and says which direction is disabled, and the title is announced when it changes (`PeriodNav.tsx`, #1218).
